verses.26:1: O Senhor é a minha luz e a minha salvação, * a quem temerei?
verses.26:2b: Os que me atribulam, os meus inimigos, * eles mesmos se enfraqueceram, e caíram.
verses.26:3b: Se uma batalha se levantar contra mim, * {inhoc}.
verses.26:4: Uma coisa pedi ao Senhor, {requiram}, * {ut} na casa do Senhor todos os dias da minha vida:
verses.26:4b: {utveja} {voluptas} do Senhor, * e visite o seu templo.
verses.26:5: Porque ele me escondeu na sua tenda: * no dia dos males me protegeu {abscondito}.
verses.26:6: {petra}: * e agora exaltou a minha cabeça sobre os meus inimigos.
verses.26:6b: Andei ao redor, e imolei na sua tenda {hostia}: * cantarei, e entoarei um salmo ao Senhor.
verses.26:7: Escutai, Senhor, a minha voz, com que clamei a vós: * tende piedade de mim, e escutai-me.
verses.26:8: A vós disse o meu coração, {facies}: * a vossa face, Senhor, {requiram8}.
verses.26:9: Não desvieis de mim a vossa face: * {declines}.
verses.26:10: Porque o meu pai e a minha mãe me abandonaram: * o Senhor, porém, me recolheu.
verses.26:11: {legem}: * e encaminhai-me à vereda reta por causa dos meus inimigos.
verses.26:12: Não me entregueis {animas}: * porque se levantaram contra mim testemunhas iníquas, e a iniquidade mentiu {sibi}.
verses.26:14: {aguarda}, porta-te como homem: * {confortetur}, e espera pelo Senhor.

decisions.why: hoc is neuter. It can be ‘this’ (the situation, or the Lord just named) or the battle, since prǽlium is neuter too. The Latin leaves it open; ‘nesta batalha’ closes it, and MS1932’s ‘mesmo então’ drops the thing hoped in. speráre here is not speráre in (D36’s esperar em): the in belongs to hoc. ego is named so the hope is not heard as the battle’s.

decisions.why: Both ut-clauses are what is asked (LXX τοῦ κατοικεῖν, τοῦ θεωρεῖν; DRB ‘that I may dwell … That I may see’), not the purpose of the asking. Ps 22:6b’s formula is para que eu habite, and the glossary says 26:4 must copy it, then records the departure: after ‘uma coisa pedi … esta procurarei’, para que is heard as asking in order to dwell. The words after the conjunction stay 22:6b’s. The same que governs 26:4b, so the two requests stay one construction.

decisions.why: petra is rocha, kept apart from lapis → pedra (117:22). The Latin has no article; uma is the indefinite Portuguese needs. in is ‘on / in’ (ἐν πέτρᾳ; DRB ‘upon a rock’). Sobre says the lifting the verb already says; Numa keeps the Latin’s in and leaves super for the enemies in the next colon. The glossary row prints Sobre and tells 60:3 to copy it, so that is the ruling; Numa stays selectable. MS1932’s pedra would merge petra with lapis.

decisions.latin: Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua
decisions.why: The Hebrew is ‘teach me your way’, and MS1932 follows it (Ensina-me … o teu caminho). The Latin follows the LXX, νομοθέτησόν με … τῇ ὁδῷ σου: legem is the object, in via tua is ablative of place. D38 records that this syntax is not 118:33’s, where viam is the object. Ponde-me keeps the dative mihi on an enclitic (D13). The second colon is not part of the fork: dírige me is encaminhai-me, as 24:5 (dirigi-me is ‘I made my way’), sémitam is vereda (D15), rectam is reta so it does not spend déxtera.

decisions.why: The infinitive vidére is not a present act of seeing. Creio ver is heard as ‘I think I see’, which is why a Latinist’s Creio ver was refused and the clause Creio que verei kept: the hope is future, the believing is now. The Hebrew opens with ‘unless’ (a counterfactual); the LXX is πιστεύω τοῦ ἰδεῖν and the Latin follows it, so no se não. bona is os bens (DRB ‘the good things’; MS1932 os bens), not maravilhas. vivéntium is dos vivos.

decisions.why: exquírere and requírere are one Greek verb (ἐκζητέω), and the glossary merges them into procurar, apart from quǽrere → buscar. The stylist wants buscar for requíram so that procurar stays with exquisívit, and so that 26:8 does not chime procurou / procurarei. That chime is not a rhyme the check flags, and buscar would spend quǽrere. The two tenses of one verb stay (procurou / procurarei).

choices.26:1: illuminátio → luz (glossary; iluminação would make God a process, and the Monday Prime antiphon can still open A minha luz). salus → salvação (D6). The copula é is supplied (D2). quem as object takes a.
choices.26:1b: Length +3 accepted: the copula é, taken from both readers (draft 1’s apposition was heard as a vocative). protéctor → protetor. trepidáre → tremer; a quo is diante de quem. The neighbouring rhyme -erei is the Latin’s own echo (timébo / trepidábo).
choices.26:2: Length +5 accepted: Enquanto is three syllables for dum’s one, and malfeitores is the glossary noun. édere stays comer; devorar (MS1932) is a stronger word than the Latin. carnes stays plural (glossary). The colon ends on a colon, as the Latin’s sentence runs on.
choices.26:2b: tribuláre → atribular, the same words as 12:5b, with inimíci mei in apposition and the article. ipsi → eles mesmos. infirmári → enfraquecer-se, the middle already used at 17:37 (the passive foram enfraquecidos asks for an agent the Latin does not name). cádere → cair.
choices.26:3: Length +4 accepted: acampamento is five syllables for castra’s two. Draft 2 takes assentar (the camp pitches) and ends the colon on the camp, where castra stands. The future non timébit is kept, and the heart stays last.
choices.26:3b: exsúrgere advérsum → levantar-se contra, the same turn as the camp in 26:3. prǽlium → batalha.
choices.26:4: Length +3 accepted: coisa is the noun Portuguese needs for unam, and esta already marks it as the one request (só, MS1932, is not in the Latin). pétii perfect, requíram future: pedi / procurarei. requírere → procurar (glossary). domus → casa. ómnibus diébus is todos os dias, not o dia todo (that is tota die). The second colon matches the Latin’s 21.
choices.26:4b: visitáre → visitar. templum → templo, with the article.
choices.26:5: abscóndere → esconder; tabernáculum → tenda (glossary; tabernáculo is a church’s in Brazil, and it is a proparoxytone at both cadences). ele is supplied so the first colon is not left short. in die malórum stays no dia dos males (plural). in abscóndito → no lugar escondido; the stylist’s esconderijo is the option (it is latíbulum’s). Both cola end on tenda: the Latin ends both on the tent, so the rhyme is kept.
choices.26:6: Length +3 on the second colon accepted: agora for nunc, cabeça for caput, and the articles on the possessives. exaltáre → exaltar, both times. super → sobre.
choices.26:6b: Length +4 on the second colon accepted: D25’s entoar um salmo is two words for psalmum dicam. Circuívi has no object, so Andei ao redor. immoláre stays imolar. vítima de aclamação was heard as ‘victim of acclaim’ by the stylist and the ambiguity reader; sacrifício de aclamação is the option and spends sacrifícium. cantáre stays cantar.
choices.26:7: exaudíre → escutar (D3): Escutai … e escutai-me. The enclitic on the second is how exáudi me is said (118:145). miseréri → tende piedade de mim. qua → com que. ad te, God, is a vós. clamáre → clamar, perfect.
choices.26:8: Tibi is a vós. The heart’s saying is not turned into a quotation: the Latin gives no speech, only a second indicative. The procurou / procurarei chime is the cost of one verb for exquírere and requírere; buscar is the option and spends quǽrere.
choices.26:9: Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me follows 12:1’s words with the negation. Draft 2 moves the servant before the wrath, so na ira is not heard as the servant’s anger. com ira is the stylist’s option.
choices.26:9b: Length −4 accepted: the Portuguese verbs are shorter, and nothing faithful can be added. derelínquere → abandonar. despícere → desdenhar, apart from spernere → desprezar (21:25); the stylist’s desprezeis is the option. The Latinist’s ajudador is the option under D24. auxílio at the mediant is paroxytone.
choices.26:10: dereliquérunt, the same verb, → abandonaram. autem after the subject: o Senhor, porém. assúmere (me) → recolher (glossary; MS1932 has the same word). tomar consigo is the row’s other candidate.
choices.26:11: The second colon is glossary throughout: encaminhai-me (24:5; dirigi-me is ‘I made my way’), à vereda (D15; in + accusative), reta (not direita, which is déxtera), por causa dos meus inimigos (propter, as 5:9).
choices.26:12: Length +5 on the second colon accepted: testemunhas, iniquidade and a si mesma are the Latin’s own words and the responsory has to say them. insúrgere in → levantar-se contra (glossary). testes iníqui → testemunhas iníquas (iníquus → iníquo). The responsory is this colon and has to stand alone.
choices.26:13: in terra vivéntium → na terra dos vivos. viventes would also be paroxytone; vivos is the plainer word. The antiphon of the Office of the Dead is this verse.
choices.26:14: Length +5 accepted: D36’s three verbs and the jussive que. The addressee is a singular human, so tu (rule 3). Aguarda can be heard as ‘the Lord waits’; porta-te, in the same colon, shows the imperative, and Aguarda tu is the option. The inverted fortaleça-se is the option; 30:25 copies the que. viríliter ágere → porta-te como homem.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from the DO Latin, LXX, DRB and MS1932. No Diurnal: Ps 26 is not in the day hours. Hebrew not followed where the Latin follows the LXX: 26:8 the face sought (indicative), 26:11 a law set in the way, 26:13 an affirmative credo, 26:12 the iniquity lying to itself. Hard readings recorded as decisions: the camp, hoc, the ut-clauses, voluptas, petra, hostia, the face, declinare, adjutor, salutaris beside salus, the law, the souls, sibi, credo videre.

Draft 1, hard pass. Soft flags accepted: 26:2 +5, 26:3 +4, 26:4 +3, 26:6 +3, 26:6b +4, 26:9b −4, 26:12 +5, 26:14 +5. The copula in 26:1b was dropped to clear +3; both readers sent it back. Rhymes kept because the Latin has them: 26:1/26:1b -erei, and tenda/tenda in 26:5.
Five remarks, one major. 26:1b and 26:9 taken. 26:4b, 26:9b and 26:13 kept, each already an option.

outcomes.remark: apposition loses ‘the Lord is the protector’
outcomes.reason: A nominal sentence, parallel to 26:1. The copula is grammar (D2). The stylist said the same.

outcomes.remark: voluptátem singular, not as delícias
outcomes.reason: Number is grammar (D2). delícias is the idiom, and 35:9 already refused the singular. a delícia was already option 1.

outcomes.remark: na ira do vosso servo reads as the servant’s anger
outcomes.reason: The order glued in ira to the servant. do vosso servo na ira keeps God’s wrath and the separative a servo tuo. Major, and two other readers heard the same misparse.

outcomes.remark: auxílio is abstract; Sede o meu ajudador
outcomes.reason: D19/D24 hold auxílio against an agent noun. ajudador was already option 3.

outcomes.remark: Creio que verei resolves the bare infinitive; Creio ver
outcomes.reason: Creio ver is heard as ‘I think I see’. The clause is how Portuguese says the future hope. The ambiguity reader did not hear a present seeing. Already option 2.

audit.note: Nine remarks. 26:1b taken with the Latinist. 26:3 taken: assentar keeps the camp and leaves the office-word. The other seven change a glossary word or a copied line, so they stay options.

outcomes.remark: bare apposition stalls after 26:1’s copula
outcomes.reason: Same fix as the Latinist. Grammar.

outcomes.remark: se instalar is administrative
outcomes.reason: assentar is the camp pitching, the same image, and the colon now ends on acampamento, where castra stands. erguer-se stays the person’s consístere (D39).

outcomes.remark: esta procurarei → esta buscarei
outcomes.reason: buscar is quǽrere’s. exquírere and requírere are one Greek verb and stay procurar.

outcomes.remark: lugar escondido → esconderijo
outcomes.reason: esconderijo is latíbulum’s. lugar escondido keeps one root with escondeu, and 30:21 copies it.

outcomes.remark: vítima de aclamação sounds like ‘victim of acclaim’
outcomes.reason: The mishearing is real, and the ambiguity reader had it too. sacrifício spends sacrifícium (115:17 has both roots). vítima stays; his line is the option.

outcomes.remark: procurou / procurarei chime; buscarei on the second colon
outcomes.reason: Same split as 26:4. The chime is the cost of one verb. Not a cadence rhyme.

outcomes.remark: não vos aparteis do vosso servo com ira
outcomes.reason: The reorder is the Latinist’s and is taken. com changes in ira; na ira stays.

outcomes.remark: desdenheis → desprezeis
outcomes.reason: desprezar is spernere’s. 21:25 sets the two side by side (não desprezou, nem desdenhou).

outcomes.remark: e que → e fortaleça-se o teu coração
outcomes.reason: An earlier stylist called the inversion ceremonious, and 30:25 copies the que. Both are grammar. The copied line stands.

audit.note: The one misreading that was not the Latin’s own is 26:9, taken with the Latinist. 26:6b and 26:14 stay open as options. The rest are the Latin’s range, or a first hearing that was already right. Unknown words kept where the glossary has already kept them.

outcomes.remark: enquanto: while they approach, or at the time they approached
outcomes.reason: dum with the present is ‘while’. The first hearing is the right one.

outcomes.remark: carnes: devour me, or literal meat
outcomes.reason: The plural image is the Latin’s (D2). The first hearing was the figurative one.

outcomes.remark: acampamento: a siege camp, or a campsite
outcomes.reason: First hearing was the army camp, helped by contra mim. That is castra.

outcomes.remark: não temerá o meu coração: heart as subject or object
outcomes.reason: First hearing was the subject, which is the Latin.

outcomes.remark: nisto: the Lord, the battle, or ‘I will wait’
outcomes.reason: hoc is neuter and the Latin leaves it open. Closing it is already the options of inhoc. esperar here is not esperar em.

outcomes.remark: esta procurarei: seek, or look for something lost
outcomes.reason: First hearing was ‘this is what I will seek’. buscar is the stylist’s option on requiram.

outcomes.remark: delícias: the Lord’s delight, or food and luxuries
outcomes.reason: First hearing was the Lord’s delight. The food echo is the word’s cost; the singular is already an option of voluptas.

outcomes.remark: visite: go to the temple, or a short visit, or inspect
outcomes.reason: visitáre has that range. First hearing was going to the temple.

outcomes.remark: dia dos males: trouble, or sins and illness
outcomes.reason: malórum is open that way. First hearing was the day of trouble. Don’t resolve it.

outcomes.remark: sua tenda: the Lord’s, or someone else’s
outcomes.reason: First hearing was the Lord’s tent.

outcomes.remark: exaltou: set me high, or praised me
outcomes.reason: First hearing was the lifting. exaltar stays the glossary verb; the rock in the same colon keeps it physical.

outcomes.remark: cabeça sobre os inimigos: victory, or a physical lifting
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s image is the lifting, which is the victory. Don’t explain it.

outcomes.remark: Andei ao redor: around the altar, or aimlessly
outcomes.reason: The Latin has no object. Supplying the altar is MS1932’s parenthesis. The unclarity is the Latin’s.

outcomes.remark: vítima de aclamação: a shout-offering, or a person harmed by acclaim
outcomes.reason: The wrong hearing is real. sacrifício spends another Latin word, so vítima stays and his line is the option.

outcomes.remark: na sua tenda: the Lord’s
outcomes.reason: First hearing was the Lord’s tent.

outcomes.remark: the heart’s words: a quotation, or two statements
outcomes.reason: The Latin has two indicatives, not the Hebrew’s command. First hearing was two statements. The quotation is the warned option of facies.

outcomes.remark: na ira do vosso servo: God’s wrath, or the servant’s anger
outcomes.reason: The second reading is a misparse, not the Latin’s openness. The servant now comes before na ira.

outcomes.remark: recolheu: took me in, or gathered me away
outcomes.reason: First hearing was ‘took me in’, which is assúmere. Glossary.

outcomes.remark: Ponde-me uma lei: a law for me, or place me, or an obstacle
outcomes.reason: First hearing was a law for walking the way, which is the Latin. Ponde uma lei para mim is already option 1 of legem.

outcomes.remark: por causa dos meus inimigos: they are watching, or they caused it
outcomes.reason: propter is ‘on account of’, and the Latin leaves the shade open.

outcomes.remark: às almas: their will, or literal souls
outcomes.reason: The souls are the Latin’s image (εἰς ψυχάς). mercê and vontade explain it and are already options of animas.

outcomes.remark: mentiu a si mesma: the lie turned on itself, or self-delusion
outcomes.reason: sibi is ‘to itself’, and the Latin leaves the shade open. contra si is already an option of sibi.

outcomes.remark: os bens: good things, or possessions
outcomes.reason: bona is open that way. First hearing was the good things.

outcomes.remark: terra dos vivos: this life, or heaven
outcomes.reason: The phrase is open. Don’t resolve it.

outcomes.remark: Aguarda o Senhor: wait, or ‘the Lord waits’
outcomes.reason: The homograph is real. D36 and 36:34 fix the bare Aguarda; porta-te shows the imperative in the same colon. Aguarda tu is the option.

outcomes.remark: porta-te como homem: be brave, or behave like a male
outcomes.reason: First hearing was ‘be brave’, which is viríliter. The Latin’s vir stays.

outcomes.remark: o teu coração: himself, or a listener; the shift from vós
outcomes.reason: The Latin itself changes to tu. A singular human addressee is tu (rule 3).

outcomes.remark: unknown: atribulam
outcomes.reason: tribuláre → atribular is the glossary verb, already kept after the same report in Pss 3, 12 and 22.

outcomes.remark: unknown: imolei
outcomes.reason: immoláre stays imolar, apart from sacrificáre. The unknown verb is the recorded cost.

outcomes.remark: unknown: aclamação
outcomes.reason: vociferátio → aclamação. júbilo is jubilátio’s.

outcomes.remark: unknown: aparteis
outcomes.reason: declináre a → apartar-se de, kept apart from desviar, which this verse has just used.

outcomes.remark: unknown: desdenheis
outcomes.reason: Listed unknown again. desprezar would merge spernere (21:25), so desdenhar stays and desprezeis is the option.

outcomes.remark: unknown: vereda
outcomes.reason: D15. Kept after the same report in Pss 8, 17, 22 and 24.

outcomes.remark: unknown: atribulam
outcomes.reason: The same verb as 26:2b. Glossary.

outcomes.remark: unknown: porta-te
outcomes.reason: portar-se is ordinary Portuguese. The glossary’s line, and 30:25’s plural.

audit.note: v2: copula restored in 26:1b; 26:9 servant before the wrath; 26:3 assentar, cadence on the camp. Seven stylist lines and three Latinist lines kept as options. Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json. Checks on v2 exit 0. 26:1b is +3 again, accepted with the copula. The other soft flags stand as in the choices.
